STUDIO LEDGER · Q3 2024
The quarter, read in figures and in feeling.

A measured account of how the portfolio performed between July and September — occupancy held by season, average rates lifted by deliberate restraint, and revenue per available room narrating the quiet ascent of the studio's nine stays.

READING ONE · OCCUPANCY
A summer held its breath, and the rooms stayed full.

Mid-August carried the season's high tide — six consecutive weeks above 85% across the coastal stays. The dip into September reflects a chosen pause: maintenance windows at Tideline and Marblehead, scheduled and deliberate, not a softening of demand.

READING TWO · RATE
Rates lifted without strain, the market simply followed.

The brass-line increases announced in February — modest, footnoted, and applied across the high-shoulder months — were absorbed without resistance. ADR climbed 10.2% year over year, with the steepest gain in July at Linwood Barn, where the new sauna pavilion justified a $90 weeknight premium.

READING FOUR · PROVENANCE
Where the bookings come from, and what that says.

Direct reservations through the studio's own pages now account for two of every five nights sold — a figure that, three years ago, sat at one in five. The shift away from third-party platforms continues at the pace we hoped for: visible, but unhurried.

STUDIO NOTE
What the figures are not yet saying.

A reporting period is a narrow window. The studio's longer arc — five seasons in — shows occupancy compounding steadily and ADR keeping pace with the cost of stewarding old buildings well. Briarwood will need a full year before it earns a fair line in this ledger. Iron Mill is under quiet review; a softer winter is expected as the kitchen is rebuilt.

The next statement, December's, will close the year and tell the longer story.
